title: Aurora Effects Raster Preset Document (wave 2: bands, cycles, variants, patch anchors, ramp, base_swap, boundary)
description: Wire shape for one raster preset document, games/sonic4/data/editor/effects/presets/<preset_id>.json (aeon repo, editor-owned tree). A BAND IS NOT A SCENE FIELD: a scene is a parallax_config; the raster program is a channel of an EffectsPreset bound per SECTION (aeon docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-raster-band-ownership-design.md section 16.1), so bands live here, in the directory docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7 reserved for them. NORMATIVE for SHAPE only: which keys exist, their JSON types, and the exactly-one arm rule. NUMERIC BOUNDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT RESTATED HERE (screen-line range, CRAM address range, burst ceilings, band count, height minimum, the palette-line-0 rule): the engine's own ensures in engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp fire at build time with the measurement behind each rule, and aeon's generator forwards values verbatim so the author reads that sentence (aeon tools/EFFECTS_CONSUMER_CONTRACT.md section 2.4 at c03b9812, the consumer half this schema pairs with). Closed: any key not listed is refused; adding one is a contract change. cycles and variants were added 2026-08-30 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.2, DoD item 5, against aeon's demand artifact 8ec2b05d): they are OTHER CHANNELS OF THE SAME EffectsPreset record the raster program is a channel of (ep_cycle and ep_variants are fields of that record, aeon engine/effects/preset.emp:56-67), which is why they live in this document beside bands and why one rasterRef binds the whole of it (ruling Q1). Reserved and refused by name (still wave-2 open): fires. Known limits with NO enforcing assertion, stated so a silence is not read as coverage: nothing checks that an authored preset is BOUND to a section (an unbound preset costs ROM and shows nothing; binding is a hand-authored preset() call, BAND-FIRST-CONSUMER territory); nothing checks the total ROM cost of the preset set; the runtime variant-to-pal_line binding behind a pal_region band cannot be checked at build time (a document carrying BOTH bands and variants makes the slot half of that binding visible in one file, but no assertion is added here: ruling Q6 defers it, because an absent variants entry means the section keeps its hand-authored slot and the document is not the whole truth); nothing checks that a band is VISIBLE; nothing here refuses an empty cycles array or a variants array longer than the engine's slot count, both of which are the generator's refusals (section 7.2).

schema.description: Document format version. Absent: refused (aeon effects_gen.py load_preset).

id.description: Must equal the file's stem. Becomes the .emp label component EditorRaster_<ACT>_<id> (aeon effects_gen.py load_preset, SCENE_ID_RE). The equality with the filename is a rule of the loader, not expressible here.

name.description: Writer-owned display label, any JSON value. Read by nothing; dropped on lowering (aeon PRESET_IGNORED_KEYS).

bands.description: The bands of this program, lowered to one compose([...]). Absent or empty: refused (aeon load_preset; engine backstop raster_dsl.emp compose). The engine's program-buffer ceiling, not this schema, caps the count (three one-colour bands measured at 55 words).

cycles.description: This section's ONE palette cycle script, spelled as its array of channels: the array IS the script, because ep_cycle is one pointer (aeon preset.emp:63) and a shape must not express what the engine cannot bind. THIS IS PALETTE CYCLING (Palette_DoCycle, palette.emp:439), not the DEBUG hotkey's raster cycle table. THREE STATES, ONE SPELLING EACH (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.2, ruling Q2): ABSENT = the section keeps its hand-authored cycle, the no-cost majority case; null = cycling OFF, which lowers to the Pal_Cycle_None sentinel and never to 0; a non-empty array = the authored script. An EMPTY array is legal JSON here and refused by aeon's load_preset naming the two legal spellings, the way an empty bands is refused; that refusal is the generator's, not this schema's. The channel COUNT carries no number here (ruling Q3): PAL_CYCLE_MAX_CHANNELS is the engine's, and today only cycle_script1/cycle_script2 exist so the generator refuses more than two by name. The script's header word is derived from the array length by the wrapper and is not a document field.

variants.description: The palette variant descriptors this section binds, POSITIONALLY: index = ep_variants[i] = the slot Palette_SetVariant takes = the slot a pal_region band names in this same document (aeon preset.emp:64, palette.emp:298-319). THREE STATES PER INDEX (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.2, ruling Q5): an index the array does not reach (including an absent variants key) keeps that slot's hand-authored value, which is load-bearing because every shipped preset carries the act's water tint and a silent clear would drop it; null at an index CLEARS that slot (the engine's 'unused slots 0 = clear'); an object at an index authors it. There is deliberately no key-level null: clearing both slots is [null, null]. The slot COUNT carries no number here: PAL_MAX_VARIANTS is the engine's, locked by a power-of-two mask and three ensures, and an over-long array is refused by the generator naming it.

patch_world_ys.description: The anchor SEED per patch channel, POSITIONALLY: index = patch channel, ep_patch_world_ys[i] (aeon preset.emp:66), lowered through preset(patch_world_ys:) (preset.emp:141-148). Added 2026-09-03 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.3, DoD item 4, against aeon's key-shape artifact 81b2a719). THREE STATES PER INDEX, the variants rule: an index the array does not reach (including an absent key) KEEPS the section's hand-authored value; null at an index is the engine sentinel PATCH_ANCHOR_NONE ($7FFF, channel unused), NEVER 0; an integer authors it. UNIT: WHOLE PIXELS, absolute level space, u16, and NEITHER SIDE CONVERTS, 1:1. This is NOT item 3's unit: drift.rate is 1/256 px per frame with the editor multiplying by 256 on export; a world Y exported x256 lands 256 times down the level and the band silently never appears (aeon raster_dsl.emp:2095-2103: the screen line is anchor - Camera_Y). 0 is a real world Y, above the screen top, the most invasive state a channel can have; spell 'unused' as null. The two bounds encoded here, the u16 range and the refusal of 32767, are enforced NOWHERE ELSE today (aeon's artifact section 3, two rows marked NOTHING TODAY), which is why this schema departs from its shape-only posture for them: a closed writer-side schema is the one refusal an author meets. The array's max length is RASTER_MAX_PATCH = 4 (raster_dsl.emp:2089), encoded for the same reason (preset.emp:161/167 ensure length 4 at the call site, but the generator pads a short array, so an over-long one has no other refusal before the engine's). A seed without a motion is legal and stationary; a motion without a seed on a channel the section leaves unused is seeded to the sentinel and never shows, so an author wanting movement authors BOTH keys at that index.

patch_motion.description: The anchor MOTION per patch channel, POSITIONALLY, the same index space as patch_world_ys: ep_patch_motion[i] (aeon preset.emp:86), lowered through preset(patch_motion:) to anchor_sweep(amp_shift:, period_shift:, phase:) (raster_dsl.emp:2232-2238). Added 2026-09-03 (section 7.3, DoD item 4, aeon 81b2a719). THREE STATES PER INDEX: unreached index or absent key KEEPS the hand-authored value; null is ANCHOR_MOTION_NONE (0, no motion); an object authors it. EXACTLY ONE ARM, sweep, the single-arm form item 3's drift uses. There is deliberately NO approach arm and none is reserved: APPROACH has no preset seed field (preset.emp:81-87 scopes it out; its handle is the runtime call Effects_SetTargetY), so a reserved arm would be a key with nothing behind it. A motion is only READ in a game whose SCANLINE_CAPS raises CAP_ANCHOR_MOTION ($0100; sonic4 yes, demo no): the seed is installed unconditionally (34 bytes, preset.emp:333-340) while the latch loop that reads it is gated (raster.emp:1930), so in an ungated game an authored sweep is a silent no-op, not a refusal (aeon artifact section 4b; a generator refusal is step 4's). A sweep whose peak-to-peak travel leaves the channel's patchable(lo, hi) band is handled ASYMMETRICALLY, deliberately (corrected 2026-09-04 against aeon raster.emp at d8baf84f, key-shape artifact 3d917657 section 1): past hi the record is DROPPED and the band is absent for that frame (raster.emp:1979-1980); below lo it is CLAMPED UP and still emitted (:1981-1983), because the frame-top ship covers what is above; the record returns on the first frame the latched line re-enters [lo, hi], not at a zero crossing. This sentence is rendered verbatim as an editor tooltip (aurora presetFieldTitle), so it must stay true to the engine, and no comptime scope holds both numbers; aeon's tools/test_anchor_sweep_band.py is that scope and today reads only the hand-authored module, which is why extending it to the generated module is a hard prerequisite of step 4.

ramp.description: The dense-tier RAMP: one linear per-scanline vertical-scroll run, RasterRampProgram (aeon engine/effects/raster.emp:582-593), built by raster_ramp_program(top, lines, cmd, start, step) (raster.emp:629-678). Added 2026-09-03 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.4, DoD item 6, against aeon's key-shape artifact docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-item6-dense-perline-vscroll-key-shape.md at aeon 9e85baf0, authored at item 6's landing cf3dfb1a). ONE OBJECT, never an array: a preset has exactly one raster: channel (EffectsPreset.ep_raster, preset.emp:62/141), so there is one ramp per document. EXACTLY ONE OF bands OR ramp per document, asserted by this file's top-level oneOf: both lower into the SAME raster: slot and the engine has no combinator that mixes a sparse fire list with a dense run (artifact sections 1.5, 2, 8: no ensure refuses the pair because no code accepts it), so the contract refuses the pair here, the strict side, and WIDENS to allow both only when aeon ships a combinator and its own refusal; a schema can widen later and cannot narrow (protocol.md section 11.18's rule, applied to this file). ABSENT ramp on a bands document means what absent bands meant before: nothing (the document is the other kind); a section with no rasterRef keeps its hand-authored raster channel (effects_gen.py:1972). THE MUST NOT: a ramp authors exactly ONE linear rate (step) and ONE starting offset (start) over a top/lines span. NO per-line curve, NO independent per-line values: RasterRampProgram has one rrp_step and one rrp_start and no field that could receive a table (raster.emp:590-591; artifact section 6). A control offering per-line values would write what the engine cannot honour. WHAT AN AUTHOR SEES: a VSRAM target's value j (= start + j*step) displays on screen line top + j + 1, and j STARTS AT 1 -- the interpreter adds the step before it writes, so start itself is never emitted. A CRAM target is one line earlier: value j displays on top + j. (The N+1 VSRAM latency; re-measured in aeon docs/benchmarks/effects-p3/RAMP-EVIDENCE.md over 19 tops spanning 3..220 and 9 run lengths. INSTRUMENT, stated because no hardware referee exists on this project: these line numbers are as read on oracle's Rust core; oracle's legacy C++ core reads BOTH raster tiers one line earlier on the same ROM bytes, and it is disqualified as a referee because it disagrees with ITSELF by 79-83 of 224 rows between two identical boots, not because it is known to be wrong here. The landing line is UNPINNED in the Rust core's own recon (oracle docs/2026-07-16-vdp-recon.md, mid-line CRAM/VSRAM write timing an interim model), so top+2 is the instrument's reading today and not a ratified hardware fact; a one-line difference between two scanline-granularity models can be a model boundary with neither wrong about the VDP, and oracle's sub-line modelling rows are what would settle it.), and the constructor does NOT compensate; an editor preview that draws value j on line top + j is one line high. GATING: the run renders only in a game whose Game.SCANLINE_CAPS declares CAP_DENSE_TIER ($0200, scene_dsl.emp:289; sonic4 yes, demo no). The ensure lives at the CALL SITE, not in the constructor (ojz_effects.emp:1048-1049; a comptime fn's free names resolve where it is called), so the generator MUST re-emit that ensure beside every raster_ramp_program() it emits, or an ungated game builds a program the interpreter silently no-ops (artifact section 1.4, 3.3). COST, information only: 304 of the 488 cycles per scanline (RASTER_DENSE_LINE_RAMP_CYC, raster_dsl.emp:1897, measured from a two-point fixture across three boots), a build-wide ensure keeps it under the window (:1908-1909); 34 bytes of ROM per emitted program. GENERATOR OBLIGATIONS (aeon, step 4): accept a document with ramp and no bands (bands is no longer required here); lower cmd as vdp_comm(VSRAM, WRITE, target.vsram.addr), never accept a raw command word from the document; lower start and step ONLY through fp16(whole, frac256), never as a raw integer, because raster_ramp_program's start/step carry NO ensure of their own and fp16's two ensures (raster.emp:685-686) are the entire authored-range contract (artifact section 7); route the program through the same per-section chooser bands uses (effects_gen.py:2693-2694) so two raster-channel writers never race for one field; keep the ep_raster/ep_patched exclusivity (preset.emp:153-154), so a section bound to a patched: template refuses a ramp document exactly as it refuses a bands document.

base_swap.description: The mid-frame nametable-base SWAP: one OP_SET_REG raster fire on one screen line re-pointing Plane A's base register (VDP reg $02) at a VRAM address, the Batman & Robin trick, item 11a. Added 2026-09-03 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.5, DoD item 11, against aeon's shape note docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-item11a-base-swap-key-shape.md at the landing aeon 850d4c60, which SHIPPED the key ahead of this CR by its own booking's call, with a real section bound: presets/ojz_sec6_baseswap.json {line: 160, target: 57344} via section_6.meta.json rasterRef; that document reads {line: 3} since aeon 8bf6df74, the owner's 'the swap goes to the top', so 160 is the value AT 850d4c60 and not the current binding). AMENDED 2026-09-04 (T3, aeon 89ba7c5f): a LIST of band objects {plane, line, target, restore_line?} flattened into one raster program; the single-object form is REFUSED (hard break, no legacy arm); see $defs/base_swap. Still one raster: channel per preset. EXACTLY ONE OF bands, ramp OR base_swap per document (this file's top-level oneOf): all three lower into the same EffectsPreset.ep_raster channel (preset.emp:62/141) and no combinator exists; the contract refuses the pair on the strict side and widens only when aeon ships one (the ramp rule, section 7.4). ABSENT: no swap; the section's raster channel is whatever bands or ramp says, or Raster_Program_None if nothing is bound. LOWERING (aeon effects_gen.py at 850d4c60): raster_program([fire(line, [reg_set($8200 | vdp_base_reg(VdpBase.PlaneA, target))])]), the SAME three calls the hand-authored OJZ_BaseSwap makes; the generator forwards both values VERBATIM and restates no range, the engine constructs own them. NO capability bit gates it, unlike ramp's CAP_DENSE_TIER: OP_SET_REG dispatches unconditionally in every game, so no ensure is re-emitted at the generated call site; a real asymmetry with ramp, stated so nobody assumes one by analogy. NOT DEBUG-gated on the generated path: the section-6 emission is unconditional pub data reaching s4.bin (aeon measured EditorRaster_OJZ_Act1_ojz_sec6_baseswap at $013446 in the release listing, its 22 bytes identical to OJZ_BaseSwap's own program). WHAT AN AUTHOR SEES: from the swap line down, Plane A draws from the target nametable; the top of the frame is untouched, and the swap is self-restoring at the frame top (aeon item 11a on-screen captures, aeon 587873d9).

boundary.description: A patchable palette BOUNDARY: one raster fire switching a staged palette region at a screen line, moved every frame by patch channel `channel`'s world anchor; the shipped moving water, authorable for the first time. Added 2026-09-04 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.6, DoD item 4's authoring half, aeon key-shape artifact 3d917657). The FOURTH exclusive arm of the top-level oneOf: it lowers into EffectsPreset.ep_patched, the sibling of the ep_raster field the other three share, and preset() refuses both at once (aeon engine/effects/preset.emp:153-154). Absent = the section keeps its hand-authored program; no null spelling. Pair it with patch_world_ys[channel] and patch_motion[channel] in the same document to make it move. Shape and every rule: $defs.boundary.

A PATCHABLE palette BOUNDARY: ONE raster fire that switches a staged palette region at a screen line and never switches back, whose line is then MOVED every frame by a patch channel's world anchor. This is the shipped moving water (aeon games/sonic4/data/effects/ojz_effects.emp:1556-1557 at origin/master 7c1a0f78: patchable(fx_tint_band(line: 100, slot: 0, pal_line: 2, entry: 4, count: 3, sh: 1), ch: 0, lo: 3, hi: 220, offscreen_ship: 1)), and it is the shape a document could not declare until now: a band ($defs.band) is TWO fires (ON plus a derived restore) and patchable() takes exactly one (raster_dsl.emp:461-462), so the shape a document could author could not move and the shape that moves could not be authored. Added 2026-09-04 (docs/AURORA_EFFECTS_SCHEMA.md section 7.6, EFFECTS-W1 DoD item 4's authoring half, against aeon's key-shape artifact docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-channel-band-key-shape.md at aeon 3d917657, on origin/docs/key-shapes-9c-and-channel-band). LOWERING (aeon's artifact section 4; step 4 is aeon's generator): patchable(fx_tint_band(line, slot, pal_line, entry, count, sh), ch: channel, lo, hi, offscreen_ship), the SAME call the hand-authored program makes; every value forwarded VERBATIM, 1:1, no unit conversion on any field. A FOURTH EXCLUSIVE ARM of this document's top-level oneOf, exclusive for a DIFFERENT REASON than the other three are with each other: bands, ramp and base_swap compete for ONE field, EffectsPreset.ep_raster; a patchable fire list lowers into the SIBLING field ep_patched (preset.emp:62-63, via patched_program raster_dsl.emp:3576), and preset() refuses a record carrying both because whichever installs last wins DESTRUCTIVELY (preset.emp:153-154). ONE CLOSED OBJECT, never an array: one patched template per preset. ABSENT means the section keeps whatever raster or patched program it had; there is NO null spelling (a null arm would be a document with zero programs, which this schema refuses; say nothing to say none). The CHANNEL is the same index space as patch_world_ys, patch_motion and a scene's anchor.at.channel, authored and never an encoder-assigned ordinal (raster_dsl.emp:452-455): the anchor that moves this boundary is patch_world_ys[channel] seeded and patch_motion[channel] swept, so a moving water is boundary plus both positional keys at that index, in the same document. Bounds restated here are single-field engine ensures so the editor is the first refusal (raster_dsl.emp:360-361 fire, :463-467 and :475-478 patchable); TWO refusals the schema CANNOT express and the generator owes (aeon's artifact section 4): line outside [lo, hi] (:475-476), and a sweep whose peak-to-peak travel 2 * (256 >> amp_shift) exceeds hi - lo + 1 lines (today only tools/test_anchor_sweep_band.py holds both numbers, for the hand-authored module; once both live in one document the check belongs in effects_gen.py beside _check_patch_context). Travel that leaves [lo, hi] is handled ASYMMETRICALLY by the engine (raster.emp:1979-1983): past hi the record is DROPPED for the frame, below lo it is CLAMPED UP and still emitted, returning on the first frame the latched line re-enters the band. What an author sees: from the boundary line down, the named colours are the staged variant's; above it the base palette; the line follows the world anchor.

line.description: The template's DEFAULT screen line, where the boundary sits before any patch, and the line the fire is built at. fire()'s own ensure, 3..223 (raster_dsl.emp:360-361: lines 0-2 belong to the priming records), restated here; patchable() additionally refuses a line outside its own [lo, hi] (:475-476), a cross-field rule this schema cannot express and the generator must. Required, no default. The shipped water uses 100.

channel.description: The patch channel this boundary follows, 0..RASTER_MAX_PATCH-1 (RASTER_MAX_PATCH = 4, raster_dsl.emp:2131; ensure at :463-464). The SAME index space as patch_world_ys[i], patch_motion[i] and a scene's anchor.at.channel; authored, never assigned by an encoder (:452-455). Two patchable records may not share a channel (guard 11, :3144-3166 at the artifact's revision): one boundary per channel per section. Required.

lo.description: The lowest SCREEN LINE the boundary may be patched to; with hi, the band the anchor is confined to. SCREEN lines, not fire lines: the engine converts once (subq.w #1, raster.emp:1977) and an editor that subtracted 1 would be the class of bug section 7.3 forbids. lo >= 3, lo <= hi (raster_dsl.emp:465-467); the lo <= hi half is cross-field and the generator's. Required. Below lo the engine CLAMPS UP and still emits (raster.emp:1981-1983).

hi.description: The highest SCREEN LINE the boundary may be patched to. hi <= 223 (raster_dsl.emp:465-466). Required. Past hi the engine DROPS the record for that frame and the tint is absent until the latched line re-enters [lo, hi] (raster.emp:1979-1980); a sweep must fit: 2 * (256 >> amp_shift) <= hi - lo + 1, the check the generator owes once both numbers live in one document.

offscreen_ship.description: When this channel's anchor leaves the TOP of the screen, re-ship the staged colours at the frame top so the tint survives the camera leaving the band at the lo end (patchable's offscreen_ship, raster_dsl.emp:150-154, :477-478); true is what the shipped water sets. Requires exactly one stream_pal_region op on the fire (:486-487), which fx_tint_band always has, so the document cannot get this wrong. false/0 or true/1, the sh spelling (aeon _render_bool_int). OPTIONAL, default false: patchable's own default (:460).

on.description: WHAT the boundary switches: exactly one arm, pal_region, the staged palette region fx_tint_band streams (raster_dsl.emp:654-663 builds region_boundary(:436-443) from it). The region carries NO addr: fx_tint_band DERIVES the CRAM address from pal_line and entry (:657, 0 * 128 + pal_line * 32 + entry * 2), so a document carrying addr would be one fact computed twice, and $defs.tint_region refuses it by closure. A cram arm is deliberately NOT here and none is reserved: fx_tint_band takes a staged region only, and a boundary that writes raw CRAM words would be a different constructor and its own CR. A vsplit arm (the shipped program's second patchable record, fx_vscroll_split at ojz_effects.emp:1558-1559) is deliberately NOT reserved either, per the approach precedent of section 7.3: patchable's offscreen_ship requires a stream_pal_region op a vscroll split does not have (:486-487), so a reserved arm would carry a hole; adding one later is its own CR.

sh.description: Shadow/Highlight on for the boundary: false/0 = one stream op on the fire; true/1 adds reg_sh_on to the SAME fire, one fire either way (region_boundary raster_dsl.emp:438-442: sh adds an op, never a fire, which is why this shape stays patchable). Same spelling as $defs.band.sh. Required, no default, deliberately (whether an effect changes a mode register is stated at the call site). The shipped water sets it.

tint_region.description: $defs.pal_region WITHOUT addr: the four arguments fx_tint_band takes (raster_dsl.emp:654-655). The CRAM destination is derived by the constructor from pal_line and entry (:657), so addr is refused here by closure rather than accepted and cross-checked: a document is one source for one byte. Every range is stream_pal_region's own ensure (:267-281: slot 0..1, pal_line 1..3, entry 0..15, count within RASTER_BURST_MAX_DEEP and within the line) and is NOT restated, section 7.1's shape-only posture; the engine message carries the measurement.

slot.description: Which Pal_Variant_Stage slot the colours are streamed FROM; not the CRAM destination. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region (slot range).

pal_line.description: The staging source's palette line, and the line the derived CRAM address lands on. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region.

entry.description: The staging source's first entry, and the entry the derived CRAM address lands on. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region.

count.description: How many colours are swapped. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region (burst ceiling, entry + count within the line). The runtime binding of the variant to pal_line is NOT checkable at build time.

base_swap.description: A LIST of mid-frame nametable-base BANDS in document order, flattened into one raster program (aeon tools/effects_gen.py BASE_SWAP_KEYS, T3 2026-09-04, section 7.5 amended). Was one closed object with line and target (a single edge that ran to the bottom of the frame, restored only by the frame-top flush); that shape is REFUSED now, a HARD BREAK with no legacy arm (a document that parses two ways is worse than one that fails loudly; the only document in the tree migrated). Each band is one ON fire and, when restore_line is present, one OFF fire writing the plane's own home base (VRAM_PLANE_A / VRAM_PLANE_B, the engine's fact, never authored). ORDERING IS NOT ENFORCED BY THIS SCHEMA AND NOT BY AEON'S GENERATOR: the flattened fire sequence must be strictly ASCENDING across the whole list, bands included, and no band may overlap another; the AUTHORITY is fire_lines in aeon engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp, which refuses overlapping, descending or duplicated lines by name at .emp BUILD time. So a document can validate here, pass the generator's shape check, and fail at build; an editor that wants the refusal earlier derives it from this sentence: flatten every band's line and, where present, restore_line into one sequence IN DOCUMENT ORDER, do not sort (a sort destroys the evidence: [100, 50] sorted ascends, so a sorted check accepts every descending document and catches only exact duplicates), and require each entry to exceed the one before (aurora's finding, planted and measured, 2026-09-04). EDGES: line and restore_line are FIRE lines; the register changes about 45%% across that scanline, so each edge row is half one picture and half the other; the fully swapped rows are line+1 .. restore_line-1 (measured: a 3..64 band is INSIDE 4..63).

plane.description: Which scroll plane's nametable base this band re-points: PlaneA is VDP reg $02, PlaneB is reg $04. REQUIRED, never defaulted: the register IS the content of the inversion (the owner's 'foreground in the background layer at the top, background in the foreground layer at the bottom' is two registers). CLOSED to the two plane variants: VdpBase has five variants and three name the window, the sprite table and hscroll; a forwarded SpriteTable would assemble and re-point the sprite table mid-frame, and sigil cannot refuse a legal call. A document may never name a register: register and variant use different shifts (10 vs 13) and the generator pairs them by name.

line.description: The screen line the band's ON fire is on; fire()'s own ensure is 3..223 (aeon engine/effects/raster_dsl.emp:360-361), restated so the editor is the first refusal.

target.description: The raw VRAM byte address the plane's base register is re-pointed at, 0..65535 (vdp_base_reg's range, aeon engine/vdp.emp:114), a multiple of 8192 (the register granule; bits below it drop silently, so the schema refuses them).

restore_line.description: OPTIONAL. The screen line the band's OFF fire is on, writing the plane's own home base; ABSENT means the band runs to the bottom of the display, ended by the frame-top flush (the shipped single-edge shape). Must exceed line: not restated here, fire_lines refuses the inverted pair by name.

ramp.description: One dense-tier ramp, the document face of raster_ramp_program(top, lines, cmd, start, step). All five inputs are REQUIRED because the constructor defaults none of them (raster.emp:629-678); cmd is spelled as target (an arm plus a byte address) and lowered by the generator. The span bounds restate the engine's ensures so an author meets the refusal in the editor rather than at somebody else's build: top >= 3 (raster.emp:631), lines >= 1 (:632), top + lines <= 223 (:640-641, the frame-rewind interlock, not the raw 224-line screen); the sum cannot be written in this schema and is the generator's and the engine's to refuse, so the per-field maxima here (top <= 222, lines <= 220) are only the loosest values the sum admits, not the contract for the pair.

top.description: First screen line of the run. 3 is the floor (raster.emp:631); 222 is the largest value any lines >= 1 admits under top + lines <= 223. For a VSRAM target the first written value DISPLAYS on top + 2 for a VSRAM target, not top + 1, AS READ ON ORACLE'S RUST CORE (the legacy core reads one line earlier and is self-inconsistent; the landing line is unpinned in the Rust core's own model; no hardware referee exists, see the ramp description): screen lines top and top + 1 both render with whatever was live before the run. A CRAM target is one line earlier. A run of `lines` values occupies screen lines top+2 .. top+lines+1, so top + lines == 223 puts the last value on line 224 where it can never be seen -- a 220-line run from top 3 renders 219 lines (the N+1 latency, raster.emp:602-609).

lines.description: Run length in scanlines, one write per line. 1 is the floor (raster.emp:632); 220 is the largest value top >= 3 admits under top + lines <= 223. Cost is 304 cycles per line of the 488 available (raster_dsl.emp:1897, :1744).

start.description: The accumulator's value on the run's first line, in pixels of vertical scroll, spelled as fp16(whole, frac256). Lowered to raster_ramp_program's start (raster.emp:629), which the engine reads as a signed 16.16 initial accumulator (rrp_start, :590).

step.description: The per-line delta, in pixels of vertical scroll PER SCANLINE, a RATE: each line adds step to the accumulator and writes the whole part. Spelled as fp16(whole, frac256); lowered to raster_ramp_program's step (raster.emp:629), rrp_step (:591), signed. This is the ONLY per-line vocabulary a ramp has; there is no per-line curve (artifact section 6).

ramp_target.description: Where the run writes, spelled as an explicit target arm plus an explicit byte address rather than a raw VDP command word (the pal_region precedent, effects_gen.py:471-478: spelled out beats one fact computed twice). EXACTLY ONE ARM and only vsram exists in this contract: item 6 is per-line VERTICAL SCROLL, and a CRAM ramp, which the engine constructor also accepts (raster.emp:652-659), gets its own arm by its own CR when something authors one; nothing is reserved for it here (the anchor-mover rule: no arm with nothing behind it).

addr.description: The VSRAM byte address the ramp writes every line, 0..78 (engine ensure addr <= 78, raster.emp:654-655; VSRAM is 80 bytes). Plane A's whole-plane vertical scroll is 0 and plane B's is 2; per-column entries follow in pairs. Whether an ODD address is meaningful is NOT ESTABLISHED (the engine refuses only > 78), so this contract does not refuse it either; an author wanting a whole-plane scroll writes 0 or 2. rrp_mask is DERIVED as 0 for a VSRAM target and is never authored (raster.emp:660-661).

fp16.description: A signed fixed-point value spelled the way the engine's fp16(whole, frac256) helper takes it (aeon engine/effects/raster.emp:684-689), so the generator emits fp16(whole, frac256) verbatim and no raw 16.16 literal ever reaches raster_ramp_program(). THE AUTHORED RANGE IS THE CONTRACT and it is fp16's two ensures: whole in -512..511 (raster.emp:686), frac256 in 0..255 (:685). The STORAGE is a u32 carrying signed 16.16 (rrp_start/rrp_step, raster.emp:590-591) and could hold a whole part of roughly -32768..32767, about 64 times the authored range; a control built on the storage width offers an author values the build refuses. State the range, note the width, never the reverse (artifact section 7; the same rule patch_world_ys states for u16 and 32767). VALUE: whole + frac256/256, so {whole: 0, frac256: 128} is one half; a negative value is whole negative with frac256 still 0..255 and the magnitude ADDED to it, exactly as fp16 computes it ((whole * 65536) - (frac256 * 256) for whole < 0, :687), so {whole: -1, frac256: 128} is -1.5, not -0.5. UNITS for step: pixels of vertical scroll per scanline (a rate); for start: pixels, the accumulator's initial value on the run's first line.

whole.description: The integer part, -512..511, fp16's own ensure (raster.emp:686). Required, no default.

frac256.description: The sub-pixel part in 1/256 px, 0..255, fp16's own ensure (raster.emp:685). Required, no default; write 0 for a whole number.

patch_motion_entry.description: One authored motion: exactly one arm. Only sweep exists; zero arms, two arms or an unknown arm are refused here and by the generator's shape check (aeon effects_gen.py, step 4).

anchor_sweep.description: A sinusoidal sweep of the anchor about its seed, anchor_sweep() (aeon raster_dsl.emp:2232-2238), packing amp_shift, period_shift and phase into one motion word. THE LADDERS ARE QUANTIZED and the two shifts are BASE-2 LOGARITHMS, not physical units: peak excursion is 256 >> amp_shift px (7 rungs, 64 px down to 1 px), one cycle is 256 << period_shift logic ticks (9 rungs, 4.27 s to 1092 s at 60 Hz). Aurora converts DOWN on export (amp_shift = log2(256 / peak_px), period_shift = log2(cycle_seconds * 60 / 256)) and a slider must SNAP to a rung: rounding a shift instead of snapping silently doubles or halves the amplitude or the period, invisibly at author time. phase is the only continuous field. The shipped hand-authored precedent is OJZ_Preset_Sec0, anchor_sweep(amp_shift: 4, period_shift: 1): 32 px peak-to-peak over 8.53 s. Ranges are the engine's ensures (raster_dsl.emp:2232/2234/2236) and are restated here only as the rungs the UI must offer; the engine's message is the field's documentation.

amp_shift.description: Amplitude rung: peak excursion 256 >> amp_shift px, so 2 = 64 px and 8 = 1 px, powers of two only. Required, no default. Engine ensure raster_dsl.emp:2232.

period_shift.description: Period rung: one cycle is 256 << period_shift logic ticks, so 0 = 256 ticks (4.27 s at 60 Hz) and 8 = 65536 ticks. 8 is the ceiling because the tick counter is 16 bits (ANCHOR_TICK_BITS). Required, no default. Engine ensure raster_dsl.emp:2234.

phase.description: Starting point in the 256-entry sine table: 0..255 is one full cycle, phase = round(fraction_of_cycle * 256). The only optional field, because it is the only one anchor_sweep() defaults (0). Engine ensure raster_dsl.emp:2236.

top.description: Screen line the effect turns ON; the band's writes land on this line. Required, no default. 0 is not off, it is line 0, which the engine refuses (lines 0-2 belong to the priming records). Value rules: raster_dsl.emp fire (screen-line range), band (top < bot, height vs fire_cost_cycles).

bot.description: Screen line the effect turns OFF: the derived pal_restore's line. The band covers top..bot-1 inclusive; bot - top is the height the engine charges. Required, no default. Value rules: raster_dsl.emp fire, band (top < bot; height; the S/H height rule when sh is set).

sh.description: Shadow/Highlight on for the band. Required, no default, deliberately (whether an effect changes a mode register is stated at the call site). false/0 = two-fire band; true/1 = the three-fire S/H shape. aeon _render_bool_int; raster_dsl.emp band (sh must be 0 or 1).

on.description: The ON op the band turns on; the restore is derived from it. Exactly one of cram / pal_region: zero arms, two arms or an unknown arm are refused (aeon render_band_on). vsram is deliberately not an arm: a band's restore is derived from the ON op's CRAM span and VSRAM has none.

addr.description: CRAM BYTE address the colours are written to. 0 is a real address (palette line 0, the character's line), which stream_cram and the derived pal_restore both refuse. Value rules: raster_dsl.emp stream_cram (range, even, line != 0, span within the line) and pal_restore.

colours.description: The CRAM colour words in order from addr. Its LENGTH is also the derived restore's word count. Empty: refused by the engine, not here. Value rules: raster_dsl.emp stream_cram (burst ceiling), pal_restore (DEEP-class ceiling on the derived restore), fire (per-fire stream words).

addr.description: CRAM byte address the staged variant colours land at. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region (range, even, agreement with pal_line/entry), pal_restore on the derived restore.

slot.description: Which Pal_Variant_Stage slot the colours are streamed FROM; not the CRAM destination. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region (slot range).

pal_line.description: The staging source's palette line; must agree with addr's line (addr >> 5 == pal_line). raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region.

entry.description: The staging source's first entry; must agree with addr's entry ((addr >> 1) & 15 == entry). raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region.

count.description: How many colours are swapped; also the derived restore's word count. raster_dsl.emp stream_pal_region (burst ceiling, entry + count within the line), pal_restore, fire. The runtime binding of the variant to pal_line is NOT checkable at build time.

cycle_channel.description: One rotating span of CRAM entries, lowered through aeon's cycle_channel() into a pal_cycle_channel (palette.emp:150-157, palette_dsl.emp:92-100). Four fields required and one optional, which is the constructor's own split: only dir has an engine default. Value rules are the constructor's ensures and are not restated here.

line.description: CRAM line the rotation runs on, pc_line. Never 0: line 0 is the character's, which the constructor refuses. Required, no default.

first.description: First entry index within the line, pc_first. Required, no default.

count.description: How many consecutive entries rotate, pc_count. Required, no default. Value rules: cycle_channel (a minimum, and first + count within the line); the runtime treats a too-small count as a no-op.

period.description: FRAMES BETWEEN ROTATIONS, in the AUTHOR's unit: period 8 means a rotation every 8 frames. The engine's timer reloads period and rotates at 0, so its runtime cadence is period + 1 frames (palette.emp:454-461), a quirk aeon has booked a fix for; THE GENERATOR ABSORBS IT (it emits period - 1 today, period unchanged after the fix lands) so that no authored document ever moves (ruling Q7). Consequence, stated rather than encoded: the legal document range today is the engine's range shifted by one, and the generator reports it. Required, no default.

dir.description: Rotation direction, pc_dir: forward or reverse. THE ONLY OPTIONAL FIELD, because it is the only one cycle_channel() defaults (dir: int = 0, forward). The two legal values are the constructor's ensure, not restated here.

pal_variant.description: One palette variant descriptor, lowered through aeon's variant() into a pal_variant (palette.emp:130-136, palette_dsl.emp:32-49). The transform is per colour channel, clamp((c >> shift) + bias, 0, 7) on the Genesis word, applied only to the CRAM lines the mask names. EVERY FIELD IS OPTIONAL because every one has a constructor default, which is what lets the shipped deep-water variant be {shift_r: 1, shift_g: 1} verbatim. Ranges (shift width, bias sign and magnitude, the mask's forbidden bit) are the constructor's ensures and are not restated here. v_pad is not a document field.

shift_r.description: Right-shift of the red channel before the bias, v_shift_r.

bias_r.description: Signed bias added to red after the shift, v_bias_r.

shift_g.description: Right-shift of the green channel before the bias, v_shift_g.

bias_g.description: Signed bias added to green after the shift, v_bias_g.

shift_b.description: Right-shift of the blue channel before the bias, v_shift_b.

bias_b.description: Signed bias added to blue after the shift, v_bias_b.

lines.description: Which CRAM lines the derive covers, v_lines, as the INTEGER BITMASK the engine field is (ruling Q4): the 1:1 spelling is the one that cannot drift from the engine, and a friendlier form (checkboxes, a list of line numbers) is the editor panel's job, not the wire's. Line 0 is the character's and the mask's bit for it must be clear; that rule, and the requirement that the mask name at least one line, are the constructor's ensures. Uncovered lines are left as they are.
